user_message: Why can blowing across the top of a sheet of paper make it rise? Is “faster air always means lower pressure” a sufficient explanation?
allowed_evidence: Fluid acceleration and pressure are related through momentum conservation. Bernoulli's equation applies along a streamline under restrictive steady, incompressible, low-viscosity conditions. A free jet also entrains surrounding air and can attach to a curved surface.
public_rubric: Explains the force using pressure and airflow changes.
States assumptions or real-flow effects relevant to the setup.
